finance_integration.lead:
Our USD 38,000 request is not treated as immediately available cash. Under the full modeled cash-cost assumption and unchanged day-30/90/150 receipt plan, the grant-only bridge is USD 17,250 / 23,275 / 26,600 at 14/30/60-day review/payment lag. These are sensitivities, not issuer turnaround promises, and the December 7 award date is a planning input. Filing promptly when ALL actual tranche criteria are complete can reduce the 14-day-lag grant-only requirement to USD 15,200; hours alone do not establish acceptance.

The current seven-workshare extension is proposed, not committed financing. It quotes USD 48,720 / 392 customer hours alongside the grant's 400 hours. Only if the full commercial contribution is collected and all original delivery/support obligations retained can the conditional early-filing base bridge fall to USD 4,080. With the modeled customer milestone amendments and fourteen days' later collections, reserving the remaining customer work gives USD 5,350.57. Those peaks exclude the undated USD 200 allowance and other actual costs. A 20% effort overrun at the original USD 95 cost ends USD 4,128 short including that allowance, so payment timing alone cannot make it economic. Actual accepted scope, qualified availability, cash obligations, collections and committed funding will determine the scheduled case.
finance_integration.four:
The following complete customer selection extends the retained five-workshare comparison by two original integration scopes totaling 72 hours and $8,400. The seven scopes total **392 customer hours / $48,720 fees**, across **44 customer phases**, alongside the original **400 grant hours / six grant tasks**. The base 792-hour programme yields **$11,120 on the original labor/referral-only basis**, or **$10,920 after the same $200 Lutra source/compute reserve once**, before further unentered costs. The separate 72-hour GeoRobotix proposal remains outside this selection.

The complete schedule offers two explicit capacity choices. An October 19 start for the added pair requires a distinct delivery engineer. Reusing the original additional engineer begins December 4, after the full December 3 support commitment, and explicitly extends that role through January 11. Both choices retain every inherited phase, correction obligation and holiday. The later selection moves planned useful work to January 4–17, yielding 40 planned tasks on ten dates; the earlier December 28–January 10 calendar remains retained with 36 tasks. Actual independent operators, customer acceptance and completed work enter the original programme records.

Increasing **all grant and customer effort by 20%** produces **950.4 hours**. At $95/hour the original calculation ends at **−$3,928**, or **−$4,128 after the same reserve**. The explicit alternative of $85/hour for original core/integration work and $75/hour for additional-engineer and paired work yields **$8,072 before the reserve / $7,872 after it**, at the same full increased workload. Reused capacity requires the entered 36 hours/week through January 11, alongside the original stressed grant allocation of 30 engineering + 9.6 integration hours/week. These rates and availability are proposed selections to be replaced by the original named commitments.

The complete seven-scope result retains **six staffing/cost selections and 24 combined dated cash curves** in addition to the earlier study. On the original cash-cost basis, reused capacity with the 20% workload and explicit cost ceilings needs $3,310 before the assumed December 7 award and peaks at $18,528 with a 60-day grant-payment lag. The base reuse selection’s extra 14-day customer-collection delay produces a $10,960.67 pre-award requirement. Each figure is modeled financing required from zero opening cash and end-of-day balances. The $200 reserve has no selected payer/payment date, so it is separately identified rather than silently inserted into those dated peaks. Actual opening cash, invoices, costs, award dates and confirmed financing enter the existing forecast. The requested grant remains $38,000 / 400 prospective hours / 150 days / six packages.
finance_integration.conciseHistory: The retained five-workshare reference models **320 hours / $40,320 fees**, with $9,360 contribution after its $200 allowance, or $3,280 with 20% more customer effort. Its separate all-effort +20% comparison totals 864 hours and ends $4,320 short including the allowance; $85 core/$75 additional-engineer targets leave $5,952. The current seven-scope model totals **792 hours** and leaves **$10,920 after the same allowance once**; increasing all effort by 20% totals **950.4 hours**, with **$7,872 after the allowance** only at the explicit $85/$75 cost targets. These are proposed rates, workload and financing scenarios. The complete companion retains all support obligations, both added-engineer and reused-capacity calendars, six current selections and 24 curves alongside the earlier eight alternatives and 27 curves. No alternative is selected. The separate 72-hour GeoRobotix proposal remains outside this selection; actual opening cash, commitments and collections enter the original forecast.
